extracted.intended_audience: playwrights, dramatists, and readers interested in dramatic composition and literary theory
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance on composing a 'dramatic narrative' (a play-like narrative not strictly bound to stage conventions), prioritizing psychological exploration of characters over adherence to classical stage rules and performability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dramatic narrative (not stagebound)
rubrics_metrics.description: "This play is to be regarded merely as a dramatic narrative in which, for the purpose of tracing out the innermost workings of the soul, advantage has been taken of the dramatic method, without otherwise conforming to the stringent rules of theatrical composition, or seeking the dubious advantage of stage adaptation.",
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat the work as a narrative that uses dramatic techniques to probe character and inner life rather than as a text primarily engineered for performance. Explicitly permits departing from traditional stage-conventions in service of psychological depth; do not feel compelled to prioritize stage-effect or 'adaptability' if that would compromise the interior exploration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use dramatic method to trace inner life
rubrics_metrics.description: "for the purpose of tracing out the innermost workings of the soul, advantage has been taken of the dramatic method,"
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use dialogue, scene, and dramatic situations as tools to reveal characters' interior states and moral psychology. Let dramatic structure serve psychological revelation rather than merely plot mechanics or spectacle.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allowance for compressed time and concentrated incident
rubrics_metrics.description: "It must be admitted as somewhat inconsistent that three very remarkable people, whose acts are dependent on perhaps a thousand contingencies, should be completely developed within three hours... A greater amount of incident is here crowded together than it was possible for me to confine within the narrow limits prescribed by Aristotle and Batteux.",
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be aware that fully developing complex characters within the short time-frame of a play (or condensed narrative) may require crowding incidents and compressing events beyond classical unities of time/plot. This is a deliberate, defensible artistic choice when the goal is intense, rapid psychological development—but it creates a tension with plausibility and classical standards that should be acknowledged and managed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anticipate stage unsuitability and moral offence
rubrics_metrics.description: "It is, however, not so much the bulk of my play as its contents which banish it from the stage. Its scheme and economy require that several characters should appear who would offend the finer feelings of virtue and shock the delicacy of our manners.",
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize that certain choices (characters, actions, moral transgressions) may render a work inappropriate for contemporary theatrical audiences or censorship standards. If exploring socially or morally shocking material, expect resistance to stage production and weigh the value of unflinching content against potential exclusion from performance or public censure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deliberate departure from stringent theatrical rules
rubrics_metrics.description: "...without otherwise conforming to the stringent rules of theatrical composition...",
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Intentionally break or loosen established rules of dramatic form (e.g., classical unity, decorum) when such departures better serve the thematic or psychological aims of the piece. This is framed as an artistic principle rather than negligence—justify formal violations by the work's deeper purpose.
